    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersPlenty-of-wontons soupPork and prawn wontons in ginger chicken broth with bok choyHow to make it250g pork mince150g green prawns, chopped1 tbsp grated ginger, plus slices for the broth2 tbsp soy sauce, divided24 wonton wrappers1.5 L chicken stock2 bunches of bok choy, halvedMix the pork and prawns with grated ginger and some soy.Fill the wrappers and fold.Simmer the stock with ginger slices and soy.Add the wontons and cook.Add the bok choy for the last minute and load up the bowls.Proton pack vegetable spring rollsLong crisp rolls of cabbage, shiitake and glass noodles, sweet chilli to dipHow to make it100g rice vermicelli1/4 wombok, finely shredded2 carrots, grated150g shiitake mushrooms, sliced4 spring onions2 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp sesame oil20 spring rolls of wrappers1 tbsp cornflour1 L vegetable oil, for frying125ml sweet chilli sauceSoak the vermicelli in hot water 5 minutes, drain and snip into short lengths.Stir-fry the wombok, carrot, mushrooms and sliced spring onion in a splash of the oil until wilted, then add the soy and sesame oil.Toss with the noodles and cool completely.Mix the cornflour with a little water. Roll a spoonful of filling tightly in each wrapper, folding in the sides, and seal with the paste.Heat the oil to 180°C and fry the rolls in batches until golden. Drain and serve with sweet chilli sauce.Ectoplasm lime dipAvocado, edamame and lime dip with prawn crackers and cucumber sticksHow to make it2 avocados200g edamame, thawed2 limes1 clove garlic1 small bunch coriander1 bag prawn crackers2 Lebanese cucumberssalt, to tasteBlitz the avocado, edamame, lime juice, garlic, coriander and salt until smooth and very green.Spoon into a bowl.Cut the cucumber into sticks.Serve with prawn crackers and cucumber for dipping.MainsZhu's sweet and sour chicken with egg fried riceCrispy chicken tossed with pineapple and peppers, egg fried rice on the sideHow to make it600g chicken thigh fillets100g cornflour1 L vegetable oil, for frying80ml rice vinegar80g caster sugar80ml tomato sauce1/2 pineapple, in pieces1 red capsicum4 eggs600g cooked cold long grain riceCook 240g rice ahead (the day before is best), spread it out and chill. Cold rice fries and holds better.Cut the chicken into chunks and coat in cornflour.Fry in the oil in batches until crisp.Simmer rice vinegar, sugar and tomato sauce, add pineapple and sliced capsicum.Make egg fried rice from the cold rice.Toss the chicken through the sauce and serve with the rice.Times Square onion sauce hot dogsThe showdown in Times SquareHow to make itAs written, serves 4All-beef franks griddled until split, in soft buns with spicy brown mustard, sweet onions stewed in tomato and a little chilli, and pickle relish.Slice 2 onions thinly and cook in oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.Add 3 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tsp sugar, half a tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp vinegar and 150ml water and simmer 15 minutes until thick and sticky.Griddle 8 all-beef franks until blistered and split.Warm 8 hot dog buns.Fill with franks, mustard, the onion sauce and a spoon of pickle relish.SweetsZhu's fortune cookiesCrisp vanilla cookies folded around paper fortunesHow to make it2 egg whites80g caster sugar60g plain flour30g butter, melted1 drop vanilla extractWhisk the egg whites with the sugar, then mix in the flour, melted butter and vanilla.Spread thin rounds on a lined tray.Bake at 180°C in batches of a few at a time.Working fast while hot, lay a paper fortune on each, fold in half and bend over a cup edge.DrinksEctoplasm kiwi lime slime sodaKiwi, lime and mint puree over crushed ice, topped with soda waterHow to make it60g caster sugar60ml hot water4 kiwifruits3 limes1 small bunch mint600ml cold soda water1 bag crushed iceDissolve the sugar in hot water and cool.Peel the kiwifruit and blitz with lime juice, mint leaves and the syrup until smooth.Spoon into four tall glasses over crushed ice.Top each slowly with cold soda water so it foams up.Stir once and add a lime wheel.Lychee jasmine iced teaKevin ordered one for his dog, Mike Hat.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
